Marathon Petroleum dropped 0.9% today, extending a brutal two-week slide of 9%. The decline reflects a broad shift in the refining sector: a major business story from November 23rd explicitly noted that "the epic boom in refinery-related stocks is unwinding," signaling that the outsized profits refiners have enjoyed are fading. While U.S. oil prices remain solid at $89.53 per barrel and refineries are running hot at 95.7% capacity, those tailwinds are no longer enough to drive investor enthusiasm the way they did months ago.

Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East—Iranian drone strikes on Saudi facilities, Houthi attacks on refineries, and new U.S. sanctions on Iran—would normally support oil and refiner stocks by tightening global supply. Instead, investors appear to be rotating out of the trade, possibly anticipating that either tensions will ease or that crude supplies will normalize, crushing the high margins refiners have capitalized on. The timing coincides with the collapse of climate talks that failed to curb fossil fuels, which may have reinforced the market's view that the refinery boom is cyclical and nearing its peak.
